summary: Design + draft the Phase-1 MVP Solidity for the GetCourt on pallet-revive (freeze interfaces, implement modules, adversarial consistency/security reconcile)
logs: Freezing interfaces, FSM, config struct, constants for Phase-1 MVP
Implementing 12 contracts against the frozen interfaces
Adversarial consistency + security reconcile across 12 files

result.fsmSpec:
DISPUTE FSM — Phase-1 single court. States: None(0) Created(1) Drawing(2) Committing(3) Revealing(4) Tallied(5) Ruled(6) Settled(7). Settled is the ONLY terminal state. Every transition after Created is a permissionless crank (anyone may call); liveness needs one honest cranker, never the app or any specific juror. All timing is in block numbers.

JUROR LIFECYCLE (outside the dispute FSM)
- stake() payable: adds msg.value to juror.stakedAmount; sets juror.activatesAtBlock = block.number + activationDelayBlocks (each new stake re-arms the whole balance's activation — simple anti-JIT). Global totalWeight += msg.value / minStake conceptually; implement as totalStaked accumulator, weight computed on demand. totalWeight INCLUDES not-yet-activated stake (makes tau slightly conservative; documented, acceptable).
- unstake(amount): requires juror.lockedSlots == 0-locked portion free, i.e. (stakedAmount - amount) >= lockedSlots * minStake; noReentrant; native .call{value:} refund; error TransferFailed on failure.
- weight(juror) = stakedAmount / minStake (floor). Each unit is an independently claimed, independently slashed SLOT.
- A seat locks exactly minStake of the juror's stake (juror.lockedSlots++) from claim admission until that round is finalized. Max loss per seat = gammaBps*minStake/BPS <= minStake. No juror ever loses more than locked slot stake. INVARIANT.

1) None -> Created — createDispute(numChoices, extraData), caller = arbitrable app.
   Requires: 2 <= numChoices <= MAX_CHOICES(8); msg.value >= arbitrationCost(extraData).
   arbitrationCost = ceilDiv(panelSize * jurorFee * BPS, BPS - appFeeBps - protocolFeeBps)  [gross-up so jurors are paid first; denominator >= BPS - MAX_TAKE_BPS > 0 by guard].
   Effects: disputeId = ++counter (ids start at 1); store arbitrable = msg.sender, numChoices, feePool = msg.value (excess over cost stays in feePool and is refunded to the app at settlement as a credit), createdBlock, configHash = keccak256(abi.encode(config)) SNAPSHOT, drawAttempts = 0, roundIndex = 0, drawBlock = createdBlock + drawDelayBlocks. Emit DisputeCreated. Evidence: submitEvidence(disputeId, uri) is callable by anyone from Created until the dispute leaves Revealing; it ONLY emits EvidenceSubmitted(disputeId, msg.sender, uri) — no storage. State = Created.

2) Created -> Drawing — startDrawing(disputeId), anyone.
   Requires: block.number > drawBlock. If block.number > drawBlock + 255 (blockhash gone): RE-ARM — drawBlock = block.number + drawDelayBlocks, emit DrawingRearmed, stay Created (does NOT consume a drawAttempt; repeatable, but any single crank within 255 blocks of a drawBlock proceeds, so liveness holds).
   Effects: round.seed = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(blockhash(drawBlock), disputeId, COURT_ID)); round.totalWeightSnapshot = totalStaked / minStake; round.tau = tauThreshold = saturatingMulDiv(type(uint256).max, panelSize * TAU_FACTOR_BPS, totalWeightSnapshot * BPS) (if totalWeightSnapshot == 0, tau = max — everyone below threshold); round.claimEndBlock = block.number + claimWindowBlocks; round.drawTarget = ceilDiv(panelSize * ALT_FACTOR_BPS, BPS). Emit DrawingStarted(disputeId, roundIndex, seed, totalWeightSnapshot, tau). State = Drawing.
   HONESTY NOTE (document in NatSpec): blockhash is collator/proposer-grindable at the margin and the last claimant before expiry could in principle time the crank; combined with drawDelayBlocks >= 10 this is an accepted MVP randomness weakness. No secure VRF beacon exists on this chain.

3) Drawing: seat claims — claimSeats(disputeId, slotIndices[], sigs[]), juror.
   Requires per call: block.number <= round.claimEndBlock; juror.activatesAtBlock <= block.number; IEligibility(config.eligibility).isEligible(juror) inside try/catch — revert or false => NotEligible (a broken policy can never brick, it only blocks claims); arrays same length.
   Per slot k = slotIndices[i]: k < weight(juror); slot (juror,k) not already claimed this round; digest = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(round.seed, uint16(k))); sig = 65-byte (r,s,v) with EIP-2 low-s enforced; ecrecover(toEthSignedMessageHash? NO — raw digest, no EIP-191 prefix, FROZEN: ecrecover(digest, v, r, s)) == juror else InvalidSignature; vrfOutput = uint256(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(r, s))); require vrfOutput < round.tau else AboveThreshold.
   Admission: insert (juror, k, vrfOutput) into the round's sorted-ascending claim list bounded at drawTarget entries; if full, evict the current highest iff new vrfOutput is lower (evicted seat's slot lock is released). Admitted seat locks one slot (lockedSlots++). Emit SeatClaimed(disputeId, roundIndex, juror, k, vrfOutput).
   HONESTY NOTE: ECDSA signing is nonce-malleable, so a juror can grind signatures over the same digest for a lower vrfOutput. Low-s halves it but does not remove it. This weakens sortition toward "grinders get admitted more often"; tau + lowest-N admission caps the damage to seat priority, not vote weight. Documented, accepted for MVP; a real VRF replaces this later behind the same seam.

4) Drawing -> Committing OR re-draw OR terminal-default — closeDrawing(disputeId), anyone.
   Requires: block.number > round.claimEndBlock.
   If admittedSeats >= panelSize: ranks assigned by ascending vrfOutput; ranks 0..panelSize-1 are PRIMARIES, ranks panelSize..admitted-1 are ALTERNATES. round.commitEndBlock = block.number + commitWindowBlocks. Emit DrawingClosed. State = Committing.
   Else (draw failed): release all admitted seats' slot locks unslashed; drawAttempts++; if drawAttempts < maxDrawAttempts: drawBlock = block.number + drawDelayBlocks; roundIndex++; emit QuorumFailed(disputeId, roundIndex-1, reason=DrawShort); State = Created-equivalent re-arm (implement as State = Created with new drawBlock — FROZEN: state value returns to Created(1)). Else: finalRuling = defaultRuling; emit DefaultRulingApplied; State = Tallied (skip 5's tally; nobody in this round is slashed — no one was seated).

5) Committing: commitVote(disputeId, commitment), admitted juror (primary OR alternate — alternates commit speculatively).
   Requires: State == Committing; block.number <= round.commitEndBlock; msg.sender holds >= 1 admitted seat this round; not already committed this round.
   commitment = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(disputeId, juror, choice, salt))  [FROZEN formula; choice as uint256, salt as bytes32; ONE commit per juror covers ALL of that juror's admitted seats in this round; clients MUST use a fresh salt per round]. Store commitment; emit VoteCommitted(disputeId, roundIndex, juror). No state change.

6) Committing -> Revealing — closeCommitting(disputeId), anyone.
   Requires: block.number > round.commitEndBlock.
   SEATING + ALTERNATE PROMOTION (FROZEN): walk seats in ascending rank; a seat is SEATED iff its juror committed, until panelSize seats are seated or seats run out. Primaries whose juror did NOT commit are marked SILENT (they had the duty; gamma-slashed at round finalization) and are replaced by the lowest-rank committed alternates. Committed-but-unseated alternates: released unslashed, no fee. Uncommitted alternates: released unslashed (no duty). seatedWeight = number of seated seats (may be < panelSize if too few commits — quorum check below still divides by panelSize, so a thin panel cannot fake quorum). round.revealEndBlock = block.number + revealWindowBlocks. Emit PanelSeated(disputeId, roundIndex, seatedWeight). State = Revealing.

7) Revealing: revealVote(disputeId, choice, salt), seated juror.
   Requires: State == Revealing; block.number <= round.revealEndBlock; msg.sender has >= 1 SEATED seat; 1 <= choice <= numChoices; keccak256(abi.encodePacked(disputeId, msg.sender, choice, salt)) == stored commitment else RevealMismatch; not already revealed.
   Effects: tallyWeight[choice] += (number of msg.sender's seated seats); mark seats REVEALED with choice. Emit VoteRevealed(disputeId, roundIndex, juror, choice, seats). No state change.

8) Revealing -> Tallied OR re-draw — closeRevealing(disputeId), anyone. Requires block.number > round.revealEndBlock.
   revealedWeight = sum of tallyWeight. QUORUM (FROZEN): quorumMet iff revealedWeight * BPS >= quorumBps * panelSize (config panelSize, NOT seatedWeight).
   Round classification of every seat of this round: COHERENT = seated, revealed the winning choice; INCOHERENT = seated, revealed a losing choice; SILENT = (primary that never committed) OR (seated that committed but never revealed); RELEASED = alternates never seated. Pot P = (minStake*betaBps/BPS)*|INCOHERENT| + (minStake*gammaBps/BPS)*|SILENT|.
   Case A — quorumMet AND unique max-weight choice W: finalRuling = W. State = Tallied. Round finalization deferred to settle().
   Case B — quorumMet AND tie for max weight: finalRuling = defaultRuling. TERMINAL-TIE flag set: at settlement NOBODY is slashed except SILENT; all revealed seats are treated as coherent-class (unslashed + jurorFee + pot share). State = Tallied.
   Case C — quorum NOT met: finalize this round IMMEDIATELY inside closeRevealing (never revisited): SILENT seats slashed gammaBps (stake reduced, slot lock released, amount into round pot P'); revealed seats unslashed, slots released, and they split (BPS-thetaBps)*P'/BPS pro-rata by seat count as compensation (NO jurorFee in a failed round — jurorFee is paid only in the terminal round; FROZEN); thetaBps share of P' + rounding dust credited to feeSink. drawAttempts++; if drawAttempts < maxDrawAttempts: roundIndex++, drawBlock = block.number + drawDelayBlocks, emit QuorumFailed, State = Created (re-arm). Else: finalRuling = defaultRuling; TERMINAL-QUORUM-FAIL flag set (final round already finalized here; settle() only handles fees/residue); emit DefaultRulingApplied; State = Tallied.

9) Tallied -> Ruled — deliverRuling(disputeId), anyone. Requires State == Tallied.
   try IArbitrable(arbitrable).rule(disputeId, finalRuling) {} catch { emit RulingDeliveryFailed; delivered = false } — SUCCESS emits Ruling and sets delivered = true. EITHER WAY State = Ruled (the app can never brick the protocol). redeliverRuling(disputeId): allowed whenever State >= Ruled && !delivered; retries the same try/catch; sets delivered on success; idempotent (reverts AlreadyDelivered once delivered).

10) Ruled -> Settled — settle(disputeId), anyone. Requires State == Ruled (delivery success NOT required — a permanently-reverting app cannot block juror payouts).
   Settle the FINAL round against the SNAPSHOT config (configHash — Phase-1 storage config is immutable, but the read path is FROZEN to the snapshot semantics). All payouts are CREDITS to a withdrawable-balance mapping (pull pattern); no push transfers here.
   Case A (majority ruling W): per FROZEN spec — COHERENT seat: slot released + credit jurorFee + floor(((BPS-thetaBps)*P/BPS)/|COHERENT|); INCOHERENT seat: stake -= minStake*betaBps/BPS, slot released, no fee; SILENT seat: stake -= minStake*gammaBps/BPS, slot released, no fee. gammaBps >= betaBps guaranteed at deploy (non-reveal costs more than being wrong).
   Case B (terminal tie): SILENT slashed gammaBps; every revealed seat: unslashed + jurorFee + floor(((BPS-thetaBps)*P/BPS)/|revealed|).
   Case C (terminal quorum-fail): round already finalized in closeRevealing; nothing per-seat here. Case D (terminal draw-short from step 4): no seats, nothing per-seat.
   Fee routing (all cases): appFeeCut = arbitrationCost*appFeeBps/BPS credited to arbitrable; protocolCut = arbitrationCost*protocolFeeBps/BPS credited to feeSink; jurorFee payouts drawn from feePool; residue = feePool - takes - paid jurorFees (includes forfeited fees + overpayment) credited back to arbitrable, EXCEPT theta*P + all rounding dust which goes to feeSink. SOLVENCY INVARIANT (FROZEN): sum of all credits + remaining escrows <= address(this).balance at all times; settlement NEVER mints — payouts <= escrowed slashes + prepaid feePool. Emit DisputeSettled. State = Settled. TERMINAL.
   withdraw(): noReentrant; zeroes caller's credit then .call{value:}; TransferFailed reverts and restores nothing (state zeroed after successful send — implementers: zero BEFORE call, revert restores via revert semantics).

GLOBAL GUARANTEES
- Termination: from any state, <= (maxDrawAttempts * 4 + 3) permissionless cranks reach Settled; no path depends on the app, the policy, or any juror acting.
- External calls out of the core: IArbitrable.rule (try/catch), IEligibility.isEligible (try/catch staticcall), native transfers (pull-only withdraw/unstake under noReentrant). Nothing else. No owner, no admin, no upgrade path, no protocol token.
- Documented MVP weaknesses (must appear in NatSpec): blockhash seed grindable at the margin; ECDSA-signature "VRF" grindable via nonce choice; totalWeight for tau includes not-yet-activated stake (conservative). No p+epsilon-resistance claim anywhere.
result.verdict: YES — the reconciled set compiles together (verified with solc 0.8.28, viaIR=true, optimizer runs=200, the exact settings in hardhat.config.ts; zero errors, zero warnings) and satisfies the invariants. Reentrancy: every value transfer (core withdraw/unstake, SimpleEscrow withdraw) is under the custom noReentrant guard with state zeroed/updated before the .call{value:}. Never-mints/solvency: pot credited == stake actually slashed (floored, exactly conserved incl. dust to feeSink); juror fees come from the prepaid feePool, and cost's ceil gross-up guarantees feePool >= appCut + protocolCut + panelSize*jurorFee >= all payouts, so settle()'s residue subtraction cannot underflow. Max juror loss per seat = minStake*gammaBps/BPS <= minStake (gammaBps <= BPS guarded at deploy). Terminality: every post-Created transition is a permissionless block-gated crank; draw-short/quorum-fail rounds are finalized where they die and re-arm at most maxDrawAttempts (<= 3) times before the default ruling; a reverting app (try/catch + redeliverRuling; settle doesn't require delivery), a reverting eligibility policy (try/catch), out-of-horizon blockhash (re-arm, no attempt consumed), and silent jurors all cannot stall a dispute. ecrecover VRF: 65-byte sig, EIP-2 low-s, v in {0,1,27,28} normalized, recovered signer must equal msg.sender, raw-digest signing and nonce-grinding honestly documented. Economic guards: validateCourtConfig (jurors-underpaid ratio, gamma>=beta, slash caps, take caps, bounds) runs in the constructor. Caps: numChoices in [2,8], panelSize in [3,21], drawTarget <= 30 seats. The drafts had no critical fund-loss bug; the issues below were real drift/spec-compliance defects, all fixed in the returned files. A verified compiling copy also sits at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-minato-32/244d7543-2647-4ba6-9ce0-0a28b2d8b169/scratchpad/jury-check/contracts/.

issues.problem: Dead, drifted ABI surface: ArbitratorCore never imported Events.sol and declared its own inline events with different names and signatures (JurorStaked vs Staked, Tallied vs RoundTallied, DisputeSettled(uint256,pot,coherentWeight) vs (uint256,finalRuling), DrawingRearmed(uint256) vs (uint64)); Events.sol also documented a SeatSettled event the core never emits and lacked SeatEvicted which it does. Any indexer built on Events.sol would decode nothing.
issues.fix: Rewrote Events.sol to declare exactly the core's real off-interface event set (Staked, Unstaked, Withdrawn, EvidenceSubmitted, DrawingRearmed, DrawingStarted, SeatClaimed, SeatEvicted, DrawingClosed, QuorumFailed, DefaultRulingApplied, VoteCommitted, PanelSeated, VoteRevealed, RoundTallied, DisputeSettled) as file-level events; ArbitratorCore now imports Events.sol and emits these directly, with all inline duplicates deleted — single source of truth, drift impossible.

issues.problem: SortitionLib and SettlementLib were drafted but never used; the core re-implemented the same math with real behavioral drift: _computeTau used a lossy (type(uint256).max/den)*num floor approximation while the lib does exact 512-bit saturating mulDiv; _verifyClaimSig rejected v in {0,1} while the lib's documented (and tested) behavior normalizes them to 27/28; SECP256K1N_HALF and the arbitration-cost formula were duplicated. Two implementations of frozen formulas is how consensus-critical drift happens.
issues.fix: Wired the core to the libraries: SortitionLib.computeSeed/tauThreshold/verifyClaim in startDrawing/claimSeats, SettlementLib.arbitrationCostOf/slashOf/potOf/coherentPayout/feeTakes in the cost and settlement paths. Deleted _verifyClaimSig, _computeTau, the duplicated constant, and the duplicated cost math. Settlement outputs are bit-identical to the draft's (coherentPayout(0, pot, theta, n) reproduces the failed-round split exactly).

issues.problem: createDispute violated the FROZEN IArbitrator doc: 'any excess is credited to the caller's withdrawable balance' — the draft folded the full msg.value into the dispute feePool and only returned the excess at settlement, possibly weeks later, commingled with the fee residue.
issues.fix: feePool now escrows exactly arbitrationCost; any msg.value excess is credited to _credits[msg.sender] immediately in createDispute (pull via withdraw()). Also simplifies the settle() solvency argument to feePool == cost exactly.

issues.problem: _failRound emitted QuorumFailed only on the re-arm branch; a round that died on the terminal attempt emitted only DefaultRulingApplied, contradicting the event's documented semantics ('re-arms OR falls through to the default ruling') and leaving indexers unable to see the final round's failure reason (draw-short vs no-quorum).
issues.fix: QuorumFailed(disputeId, closedRound, reason) is now emitted on both paths before branching; the terminal path additionally emits DefaultRulingApplied, and the Events.sol NatSpec states this ordering.

issues.problem: panelSize * jurorFee * BPS in the arbitration-cost formula was computed on every createDispute/arbitrationCost call; with an absurd (but validateCourtConfig-passing) jurorFee the checked multiplication overflows at runtime, permanently bricking createDispute after a successful deploy.
issues.fix: Cost is computed once in the constructor via SettlementLib.arbitrationCostOf and cached in an immutable _arbCost: an overflowing config now fails loudly at deploy instead of at runtime, and every cost read is a cheap immutable load.

issues.problem: SeedNotReady and NoCommitment were documented as live revert reasons but are unreachable: startDrawing re-arms (by design, for liveness) instead of reverting when blockhash leaves the horizon, and a reveal with no commitment surfaces as RevealMismatch (NotSeated fires even earlier). Misleading docs for integrators wiring error decoding.
issues.fix: Kept both declarations for ABI stability but re-documented them as RESERVED, stating exactly which behavior replaces them in the Phase-1 core.

issues.problem: The FROZEN commitment formula keccak256(disputeId, juror, choice, salt) does not bind roundIndex, so a juror who revealed (choice, salt) in a quorum-failed round and reuses the same pair in a re-drawn round publicly telegraphs their vote (self-inflicted only; no third-party forgery since the juror address is bound).
issues.fix: Formula is frozen and unchanged; the footgun is now explicitly documented in commitVote's NatSpec: clients MUST use a fresh salt per round. (Flagged for the Phase-2 seam: bind roundIndex in the next commitment-format version.)

issues.problem: No defects found under the adversarial pass (rule() is idempotent and access-checked, pull-pattern throughout, receive() restricted to the arbitrator, openDispute forwards exactly cost); only the IArbitratorCreditPull doc slightly understated what flows through the arbitrator credit ledger after the createDispute fix.
issues.fix: Doc updated to mention createDispute overpayments in the pulled aggregate; code unchanged.
